rubrics_metrics.name: Government-established press board / code of professional conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: DRAW UP A CODE OF PROFESSIONAL CONDUCT AND IMPOSE PENALTIES ... THIS BODY, THE MEMORANDUM SAID, WOULD HAVE AMONG OTHER POWERS, RIGHT TO 'BAN OFFENDING ADVERTISEMENTS, MAKE RULES TO GOVERN THE BUYING AND SELLING OF NEWSPAPERS, MAKE REGULATIONS TO SAFEGUARD THE STATUS AND AUTHORITY OF EDITORS AND PUBLISH AN ANNUAL REPORT ABOUT THE STATE OF THE PRESS' ... 'DISCLOSE ANY FINANCIAL INTEREST WHICH THE NEWSPAPER PUBLISHER HAS IN THE SUBJECT UNDER-DISCUSSION.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum proposes a government-established press board composed of industry representatives to draw up and enforce a code, with powers including banning offending ads, regulating newspaper transactions, safeguarding editors' status, and publishing annual reports. It also acknowledges limits: 'SOME ABUSES OF THE PRESS CANNOT LEGALLY REMEDIED WITHOUT INFRINGING LIBERTY ... WE REFER TO ... DISTORTION OF NEWS, DELIBERATELY MISLEADING, IMPROPER INTERFERENCE WITH THE CONSCIENCE OF THE REPORTER AND CORRESPONDENT, AND IMPROPER DIRECTIVES TO THE EDITOR.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty checks legislation for federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: HOUSE PASSED LEGISLATION SETTING UP A SYSTEM OF LOYALTY CHECKS ON FEDERAL EMPLOYES AND REQUIRING THEM TO BE FINGERPRINTED ... APPLICABLE ONLY TO EMPLOYES AND OFFICERS OF THE EXECUTIVE BRANCH AND TO APPLICANTS FOR JOBS IN THE EXECUTIVE BRANCH. IT WOULD DEFINE LOYALTY AND SET UP MACHINERY TO APPLY THE LOYALTY TEST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key procedural elements described: (a) initial screening by the Civil Service Commission; (b) if screening disclosed 'derogatory information' the Commission would refer the case to the FBI for investigation; (c) FBI results would be turned over to a Presidentially-appointed Loyalty Review Board; (d) the employee would have the right to appeal to the Board but not beyond it (attempts to allow federal court appeals failed); (e) if the employing agency refused to discharge an employee the Board could request the President to take action. The legislation proposes an independent Loyalty Review Board (rather than one within the Civil Service Commission) and a 'single standard of loyalty.' Supporters claim the bill 'provides adequate safeguards' while opponents warn of chilling effects on federal workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and media restrictions for Chinese nationals abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: CHINESE NATIONALS ABROAD WERE ORDERED TO REGISTER WITH A GOVERNMENT ORGANISATION. THEY WERE WARNED AGAINST PUBLICATION OF STATEMENTS 'HARMFUL TO CHINA'S FOREIGN RELATIONS.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government directive requires registration of nationals abroad and warns against publishing statements that might harm foreign relations. The report also notes conversion of 18 domestic newspapers formerly owned by the Kuomintang into 'commercial organs' to operate without subsidies under elected boards of directors—an example of state‑directed reorganization and controls over the press.
